comment: The brain wire, version 8: the one protocol between a brain's driver (Go: apps/locus/keeper/internal/brainwire, which cmd/cyfr-claude-code, cmd/cyfr-codex and cmd/cyfr-acp share) and its holder (Opus.Brain.Wire, Elixir), over a `run` session of the backends service, each way one JSON object per line. A line is at most `max_line_bytes` bytes, UTF-8, the object's members exactly those its message names in `fields` (each present) and `optional` (each present or absent), each of the type `types` names: `id` a non-empty string of at most `max_id_bytes` bytes; `string` any string; `detail` a string of at most `max_detail_bytes` bytes of UTF-8; `count` a whole number from 0; `boolean`; `object` a JSON object; `ids` and `strings` arrays of ids and of strings; `content` an array of blocks, each one `blocks` shows; `tools` an array of tools, each `{name, description, parameters}` with a name of 1 to 128 bytes, a description string and parameters an object; a tool is carried, one every harness carries whole, when its description is at most `tools.max_description` UTF-16 code units (as JavaScript counts a string: Claude Code keeps no more), its parameters name none of `tools.uncarried` at their top, among their `properties`, when an object, or their `required`, when a list, directly or through what composes them there, each schema of `allOf`, `anyOf` and `oneOf`, `then` and `else`, and a `$ref` into the same document (`#` and a JSON pointer), each schema read once (a case's `names` are the names so read), (the stub's own answer members, which Claude Code's driver takes out of every call's arguments), and it is at most `tools.max_stub_argument` bytes as the stub's argument, the tool as `{description, inputSchema, name}` in the driver's JSON (Go's, its strings' U+2028 and U+2029 escaped, its parameters the line's own bytes); a line may carry a tool that is not carried, which a driver refuses, and the holder hands an outside server's tool only when it is carried, with the list's carried tools at most `tools.max_tools_bytes` bytes as those arguments, each a JSON string in one array, so that what a line carries beside them fits. `tools.cases` and `tools.lists` give tools and lists at each bound, each tool its `tool` with its description, when `description` names `[text, times]`, that text so many times, and with `parameters.description` of `pad` letters y when it names one, each with the bytes it takes and whether it is carried or fits; `config` an object of the members `config` names, each of its type; `counts` an object of exactly the four `counts` names, each a count; `model_counts` an array of `{model, counts}`, the model an id and the counts `counts`; `models` an array of `{id, name, efforts}`, the id an id, the name a string and the efforts `strings`, those that model takes; `choices` an array of `{id, name}`, both strings, the id an id; `phase` one of `phases`; `error_type` one of `error_types`; `accounting` one of `accountings`; `stop` one of `stops`; `account` one of `accounts`; `signed_in` and `signed_out` that word alone; `why` one of `endings`. A list holds at most `max_list` entries. A line that does not read so, names a `t` the other side does not take, or is past a bound, ends the session: `refuse` gives such lines, each with its reason, and `read` gives lines that read, each with what it reads as. Commands go from the holder to the driver, events from the driver to the holder. The driver's first line is `hello`, naming the version and its `boot`, fresh for each driver process; the holder ends a session whose `hello` names another version, so a driver that does not know a member of this one is never written to. A driver that ends of itself writes `ending` as its last line, before its harness is closed: its `why` is the driver's own finding, one of `endings` and never the program's words, which the holder words for the person when the end comes before the work was taken (`unanswered` a start or CYFR's tools not answered within the driver's bound, `servers_unlisted` the program's MCP servers not listed, `refused` its server or session refused, `outdated` a version older than the driver's first, `unsupported` no version the driver reads, another protocol or no way to go on with a session, `ended` the program's process ended or took no more input, `unrunnable` the program or what it runs in could not be made, `unreadable` an answer past its bound or naming no session the driver can use, `unfit` a model, effort or access the program does not take, `too_many_tools` a start's tools past what the program takes whole, as its driver measures them (Antigravity drops whole tools from a list past its budget and says nothing), `broken` a command the driver does not read or allow, or an output it could not write); its reason in words goes to its standard error alone, since it may carry a system's words, a path or the program's own. The holder keeps the first `ending` it reads and acts on no line after it, a second `ending` included, reading only on to the process's end. A driver that cannot serve the wire at all (no harness to drive) says `hello` and then its `ending`. A driver ended by the holder's close, the end of its input or a signal writes none. A `start`'s `config.access` names one of the access choices the driver lists in a `models` answer's `access`, each `{id, name}`, the name the words a person reads: the driver lists only a choice it can honour in the box, starts and resumes its harness with the native settings of the one named (absent, its first listed), and a start naming one it does not list ends the driver before anything starts. A choice is the harness's own setting and no boundary of CYFR's: the driver answers each permission question of its harness with allow, and no choice restricts CYFR's tools, which CYFR's gate decides. A delivery (`work`, `post`, `answer`) names the id the holder stored it under; `models` and `forget` an id the holder chose. The driver answers each command once: `start` with `started` or `gone`, `work`, `post` and `answer` with `accepted` once the harness's input took it or `refused` when it was not written, a `post` also with `later` (not written, since the harness takes a message only between its native turns: the post is still the holder's, which writes it again, under the same id, once that native turn's `idle` has come, and a driver that ends after `later` has taken nothing of it); a holder that restarts while it holds a post answered `later` has lost the knowledge that the program had not taken it, so the next start names that post among `pending` and the turn ends uncertain, the post never written to the program again, unless that resume answers `gone`: then the program holds no session, and the fresh start's context carries the post, written to it once, `models` with `models` or `refused` (a listing the driver started a harness for is refused while that harness's account reads signed out, and when its account could not be read, as that), `forget` with `forgot` or `refused`; the holder writes the next command only once the last is answered. `account` is what the driver read positively in its harness's own account answer for that very event: `signed_out` only the one shape that harness answers with no sign-in, `signed_in` only a sign-in, key or other provider the answer names, and no member for an answer it does not know, one it could not read or none read. A `started` may carry either, a `models` only `signed_in` and a `refused` only `signed_out`; nothing else says anything of the account, an `authentication` error, an `idle` and an event without the member included. `signed_in` says that a sign-in or key is there, never that its provider still takes it. `accepted` says the harness's pipe took the command and is not durable delivery: a post Codex accepted and then lost with its process can be missing from its transcript. `forgot` says the session's transcript and whatever holds its content are gone, each removed or proved absent, but for what a program keeps of every session in one index of its own, which CYFR never writes and its driver's documentation names (Antigravity: each session's title and summary); a diagnostic line of the harness's that names only the removed session's id may remain. Every `start` names the turn's tools in `tools`: those a new native session starts with, and on a resume those a harness given its tools again at a resume lists from then (an ACP program, whose servers are named at each new session, load and resume); a harness whose session keeps the tools it started with for its life (Codex: a resume keeps the thread's own and a `work` changes none of them, so a tool a later work adds is not one the harness can call, and an ask of one the work lacks is still the holder's to refuse); a harness that takes each work's tools (Claude Code) takes them from the `work` and none from the start. Every event of a native turn (`text`, `thought`, `said`, `own`, `ask`, `usage`, `idle`, `error`) names the `gen` its session was started with and, when the driver knows it, the `work` of the command whose line started that native turn; a native turn no command started (a background command's end) names none, and every one of those events may come so. `native` names those events: the program's own lines, which the driver writes only when its harness wrote one; the rest are the driver's own. `own` is a run of one of the harness's own tools, at its `phase`, its start or its end: `call` is the harness's id for that run, the same on its start and its end, so two runs of one tool, ended in either order, end apart, an id of the harness's that is an id the wire takes is carried as written, a newline in it included, and another is carried as the driver's own derived from it; `detail`, when the harness shows it, says in the harness's own words what the run does or changed: a start its command, else what it acts on (a path, a query), else its input; an end the diffs of the change it made; never a command's output or what a read read, cut by the driver between two characters to at most `max_detail_bytes` bytes. A call of one of CYFR's own tools is never an `own` and carries no `detail`, whether CYFR ran it, refused it or never saw it: a driver tells it by what the call is, never by whether it was matched, so nothing CYFR's gate withholds reaches the wire as what a run did. `thought` is the harness's reasoning, a `delta` at a time under the `message` it belongs to, and never part of what it `said`. A sub-agent's frames are no native turn's: a driver passes on nothing of a sub-agent's own text, tools or reasoning, and the tool call of the turn that started it is that turn's one `own` of it, whose result reaches the person in the brain's own words. `usage` names a native `result` (Claude Code: each result's own identity, which gives no order, so nothing compares two of them; its counts the result's alone) or a cumulative `total` per native thread (Codex: the thread's id, its one entry in `models` the thread's counts so far across every model it ran, under the model it runs now; totals are compared by native thread across model changes and boots, the model a total names never makes a baseline of its own, and a total below the last is a reset; a resume may repeat the last total with no `work`, which against an unchanged baseline adds no spend, and an increase no work can be given stays unattributed), exactly one of the two, and its `accounting`: `complete`, every model's counts the harness reports for it, side requests included, each counted once, in `models`; `partial`, the models whose counts read, some did not, or (Codex) every total of the session from the first line of a thread not the session's (a sub-agent's, which the driver does not pass on) or the session's own call of a sub-agent, since whether a thread's total holds its sub-agents' counts is not established, and (Codex) a resumed session's first usable total, one that carries counts, which may end a stretch a sub-agent worked in whose total's event never committed, since the driver keeps nothing across processes; `unavailable`, the harness reported none, and `models` is absent, never zeros. `models` is present exactly when the accounting is not `unavailable`. A `post`'s input to the harness carries a uuid derived from the post's id where that input takes an id the client chooses (Claude Code: its user line's `uuid`; Codex: its `clientUserMessageId`), so a result or a native turn naming the uuid names the post; an ACP program's prompt takes none, so its driver carries the uuid in the prompt's `_meta`, names in `idle.answered` the posts each prompt it wrote carried, and a resume's `held` names none: the uuid is the first 16 bytes of the SHA-256 of `uuid.prefix` followed by the id, with the version nibble set to 4 and the variant bits to 10, written in lowercase 8-4-4-4-12 form; `uuid.cases` gives ids and their uuids. A `start` that resumes names in `pending` the posts whose delivery is not known, and `started.held` names those of them the session's transcript holds: delivery evidence and no more, since a post in the transcript may never have been answered; a pending post it leaves out is not established, never proved absent. A resume replays nothing but, for Codex, the thread's last total, and goes on with nothing by itself. There is no interrupt: Stop closes the session.
